about: Every model ID each provider's list-models API returns, with exactly one status: covered (it has contract fixtures under internal/providers/<fixtures.provider>/testdata/contracts/), alias (alias_of a covered model) or ignored (with a reason); ignore_rules cover whole classes. A listed ID with none of these is NEW. go test ./internal/providers/contractwatch/ checks this file against the fixture directories; the daily AgentCC Provider New Models workflow checks it against the live APIs. See cmd/model-watch/README.md.

anthropic.note: GET /v1/models lists active and deprecated models; retired ones only on request. Deprecated models are ignored from their lifecycle metadata, so only covered ones need an entry. The SDK's undated aliases (claude-haiku-4-5) are not listed, so they have no alias entries.

azure.note: Azure OpenAI serves deployments a resource owner names, not models: GET /openai/models lists what a resource could deploy, not what the gateway calls, and the fixtures key on deployment names. Only the coverage check applies; new OpenAI models reach Azure after the openai section has seen them.

bedrock.note: ListFoundationModels + ListInferenceProfiles (SYSTEM_DEFINED) in the workflow's region (AWS_REGION, default us-east-1); entries assume that region lists us. and global. profiles. Metadata ignores models that are LEGACY, have no TEXT output, are provisioned-throughput only, or are invocable only through a profile (the profile is listed instead). Base IDs (InvokeModel) and profiles (Converse) are different contracts, so us.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5 is not an alias of anthropic.claude-opus-5-5. The vendor rules exist because the adapter sends every ID that is not an inference profile to InvokeModel with an Anthropic Messages body (bedrock.go ChatCompletion), so a non-Anthropic base ID cannot work; delete them when the adapter routes base IDs by vendor.

fireworks.note: Fireworks is an aggregator: GET /inference/v1/models lists every third-party model it routes (its serverless catalog plus the account's own deployments), all answered in Fireworks's one OpenAI-compatible envelope, so a listing would report hundreds of routes, not new response shapes. The envelope is pinned by the covered model below and re-recorded by -newest (with FIREWORKS_API_KEY); the models themselves are tracked in their makers' sections. model-watch has a lister for it (sections.go): switching this section to list "api" is a registry edit, once ignore rules can narrow the catalog.

mistral.note: GET /v1/models on api.mistral.ai, with MISTRAL_API_KEY. The openai suite files Mistral's models as mistral@<model>. Mistral lists every alias (mistral-large-latest) beside the dated model it points at, and its capabilities, deprecation and type: a model whose capabilities name only endpoints the gateway does not parse (moderation, classification, completion_fim, audio_transcription_realtime: none of completion_chat, ocr, audio_transcription or audio_speech, and not an embedding model, which sets no flag), a fine-tune, or a model with an announced deprecation is ignored from that metadata, unless it is covered. Chat, OCR, embedding, transcription and speech models are contract targets (mistral-large-latest, mistral-ocr-latest, mistral-embed, voxtral-mini-latest and voxtral-mini-tts-3 cover them). The covered fixtures key on the -latest aliases the gateway's users send; when the dated model behind one changes, the new dated ID shows as NEW (consider an alias entry).

openai.note: GET /v1/models has no capability flags, so classes no contract case covers are ignored by ID pattern. Chat, completions, embeddings, images, speech, transcription and translation models are contract targets: each class has a covered template. A model with an announced shutdown_date is ignored from that metadata unless it is covered.

openrouter.note: OpenRouter is an aggregator: GET /api/v1/models lists every third-party model it routes (several hundred, from dozens of vendors), all answered in OpenRouter's one OpenAI-compatible envelope, so a listing would report hundreds of routes, not new response shapes. The envelope is pinned by the covered model below and re-recorded by -newest (with OPENROUTER_API_KEY); the models themselves are tracked in their makers' sections. model-watch has a lister for it (sections.go): switching this section to list "api" is a registry edit, once ignore rules can narrow the catalog.

perplexity.note: Sonar's chat completions have no list API: Perplexity's GET /v1/models (perplexity-py client.models.list) lists the Agent API's models. This list was assembled on 2026-10-28 from internal/modeldb/litellm.json's current perplexity/* chat entries, because docs.perplexity.ai was not reachable from the authoring session: verify it against the source page. model-watch reminds when static.checked is older than 90 days. pplx-embed-v1-0.6b (POST /v1/embeddings) and openai/gpt-5.4 (POST /v1/responses, the Agent API) are added by hand: the first is generated/api.py's EmbeddingsRequestInput.model literal and the second the model of the SDK's own responses test (perplexityai/perplexity-py@1a79c5d3a7b1ef8c2dce17c0f0aa7e23f9bbdced tests/test_generated_api_integration.py).

replicate.note: Replicate is not OpenAI-compatible: GET /v1/models answers a page of Replicate models ({next, previous, results}, gap RP1), which the OpenAI lister reads as empty, and the preset reaches no other OpenAI endpoint. The covered entry pins that page; Replicate's models are not contract targets of this gateway.

together.note: Together is an aggregator: GET /v1/models lists every third-party model it routes (about two hundred open-weight chat, image, embedding and audio models), all answered in Together's one OpenAI-compatible envelope, so a listing would report hundreds of routes, not new response shapes. The envelope is pinned by the covered model below and re-recorded by -newest (with TOGETHER_API_KEY); the models themselves are tracked in their makers' sections. model-watch has a lister for it (sections.go): switching this section to list "api" is a registry edit, once ignore rules can narrow the catalog.

vertex.note: The gemini adapter in Vertex AI mode; the gemini suite files its fixtures as vertex@<publisher model>. Vertex AI's publisher-model listing needs a short-lived OAuth access token (gcloud auth print-access-token), which a repository secret cannot hold, so it is not listed: new Gemini models are noticed by the gemini section (AI Studio) and reach Vertex AI under the same publisher model ID. The IDs below are Vertex publisher model IDs.

xai.note: GET /v1/models on api.x.ai, with XAI_API_KEY (the spec's ListModelsResponse, pinned as contractspec/subsets/xai/models). The openai suite files xAI's models as xai@<model>. latest is the alias every example of xAI's spec names; v1 is the embedding model the spec's example names (xAI lists embedding models at GET /v1/embedding-models, which model-watch does not read).
